reference: Michael's direct bosses at Dunder Mifflin, in order: Ed Truck (his predecessor/old boss, Scranton manager before him), Jan Levinson (VP Northeast region, his boss S1-S3 until fired at the end of S3), David Wallace (corporate CFO and later CEO, above Michael throughout and his direct boss after Jan), Ryan Howard (briefly VP Northeast sales, S4 only, 'I'm your boss'), Charles Miner (new VP Northeast, S5E18, whom Michael quit over), and Jo Bennett (CEO of Sabre after it bought Dunder Mifflin, S6E14-on). Michael himself lists 'David, Charles, Jan, Ed Truck' as his bosses (S7E8). Optional/debatable: Gabe (Sabre corporate liaison, chain of command in S7 although Michael insists 'Gabe is not the boss'), Robert California (CEO who arrives only after Michael has left), Alan Brand (company CEO seen once at a shareholder meeting in S6E10), Mr. Figaro (joke 'other boss' at his second job).

evidence.line: Michael: Better men than Gabe have tried to be my boss. David got fired. Charles got fired. Jan went crazy. Ed Truck, who I liked, got decapitated.
Michael: ... My old boss Ed Truck has died.
Jan: ... Ed Truck, your old boss, threatened ...
Michael: My boss is coming in today, the lovely Jan Levinson-Gould ...
Jan: ... your branch is currently number four of the five branches that I oversee.
Michael: ... my boss's boss's boss, the CFO ... is having a little shindig for all the managers
Michael: Jan got fired. And I realized that I could not work for a company that would fire my girlfriend.
Ryan: ... I know I used to be a temp here, but now everything is different. I'd like your respect. I am your boss now.
Ryan: I'm your boss. (replying to Michael's 'my boss can back you up')
Michael: ... my old temp is now my boss, so, gives you an idea of how quickly you can move up
Michael: ... Sir Charles Miner and he is the new VP for the Northeast region.
Michael: [gets up to shake David's hand] I quit.
Michael: Today, Jo Bennett, the CEO from Sabre, is coming to see us here for the first time.
Jo: ... I am CEO of Sabre International ...
Michael: ... if you have something to say, it goes through me, and then I take it to Gabe. Chain of command.
Michael: What? No Gabe is... Gabe is not the boss.

list_items.item: Jan Levinson (VP Northeast, boss S1-S3, fired end of S3)
David Wallace (CFO/CEO, corporate boss; Michael quits to him in S5E18)
Ed Truck (prior regional manager / Michael's old boss, only past tense; Ed appears S2E14)
Gabe Lewis (Sabre corporate liaison; chain of command in S7, Michael denies he is the boss)
Robert California (CEO, arrives S7E24 after Michael has left, not his boss on screen)
Alan Brand (company CEO at shareholder meeting, S6E10)

caveats: Core list follows Michael's own S7E8 roll call (David, Charles, Jan, Ed Truck) plus Jo Bennett. Ed Truck was Michael's old boss per S3E4/S4E2, but appears on screen only as a past figure (S2E14 meeting). Ryan is a legitimate boss in S4 but short-lived and comedic, so optional. Whether acting/corporate heads like Gabe, Alan Brand or Robert California count is a judgment call. Titles come from dialogue; the transcripts do not state a formal org chart.
question: Who were Michael's bosses over the series?
